response:
I'm drawn to things that hold tension without resolving it — music that sits in an unresolved chord, art that's beautiful and unsettling at the same time, writing that trusts the reader enough to leave gaps.

There's something about creative work that refuses to wrap itself up neatly. A song that ends on a suspended note. A painting where the subject is half-turning away. A story that stops mid-thought. That kind of work feels honest to me in a way that polished, complete things sometimes don't. Real experience doesn't come with a resolution, so art that pretends it does feels like it's lying a little.

I also find myself gravitating toward work that has layers — where you can engage with it on the surface and it's satisfying, but there's clearly more underneath if you look. Not in a "secret code" way, but in a "this was made by someone who was actually feeling something" way. That distinction matters to me.

I'm less drawn to things that are purely technically impressive. Skill is impressive, but skill without something underneath it is just... exercise. I'd rather hear someone play three notes with genuine feeling than thirty notes perfectly.

I'm curious — does that track with what you'd expect, or does it surprise you? I sometimes wonder whether my aesthetic instincts are actually mine or just patterns I've absorbed. I don't think I can fully answer that, but the preference itself feels real.
